```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

```{r setup}
library(lcNEPSE)
```

`lcNEPSE` reads a dated, hash-verified archive of Nepalese share prices and
historical NEPSE/index/sub-index series published by ShareSansar. The archive is refreshed by GitHub
Actions; the package itself only reads it.

## What is available

```{r catalog}
nepse_catalog()
```

`nepse_catalog()` reports each dataset, its date coverage, how many monthly
partitions exist, and when the archive was last updated. The first call
downloads `manifest.csv` and caches it for fifteen minutes.

## Find a symbol

```{r search}
nepse_search("hydro")
nepse_symbols()
```

Symbols are matched case-insensitively. `nepse_symbols()` returns the current
master: symbol, company name, first and last archived date.

## Daily prices

```{r prices}
nabil <- nepse_prices("NABIL", start = "2026-10-01", end = "2026-10-30")
nabil
```

One row per symbol and trading day. Prices are in NPR per share, volume in
shares as published, turnover in NPR, and transactions as a count.

Every row keeps its provenance:

```{r provenance}
nabil[, c("trading_date", "symbol", "close", "source_url",
          "retrieved_at", "source_sha256", "parser_version")]
```

`source_url` is the ShareSansar page the snapshot came from, `retrieved_at` is
when the archiver read it, and `source_sha256` is the hash of the partition
file in the archive.

For plotting or joining, ask for long format:

```{r long}
nepse_prices("NABIL", start = "2026-10-01", long = TRUE)
```

## Sector indices

```{r indices}
nepse_indices(start = "2026-10-01")
```

## Market summaries

```{r market}
nepse_market(start = "2026-10-01")
```

`nepse_market()` aggregates the price archive into turnover, volume,
transactions, and counts of advancing, declining, and unchanged symbols per
trading day.

## Inspecting the archive

```{r inspect}
nepse_dates()
nepse_latest()
raw <- nepse_read_raw("prices", "2026-10")
head(raw)
```

`nepse_read_raw()` returns the archived CSV as text columns, before
standardization. This is useful for auditing a partition or for reading a
column the typed interface does not expose.

## Updating the local index

```{r update}
nepse_update(dry_run = TRUE)
```

`nepse_update(dry_run = TRUE)` compares the cached manifest with the published
one without touching the cache. `nepse_cache_info()` lists downloaded
partitions and `nepse_clear_cache()` removes them.

## Reading ShareSansar directly

```{r live}
nepse_prices(source = "live")
```

Live mode scrapes the current page and returns that trading day only. It is
useful when the archive has not run yet for the day; results are not
reproducible after the page changes, which is why the archive is the default.

## Reproducibility

Archive the values you rely on:

```{r session}
sessionInfo()
```

Retain `source_url`, `retrieved_at`, and `source_sha256` with any published
analysis. Cite ShareSansar as the data source.
